causalFinding.whyExpensive: One terminal advisory ensemble runs a nominal 600 s shadow plus two 360 s stress shadows; cloned TAEM guidance repeatedly invokes its own terminal candidate planner.
causalFinding.independentCpuSample: Hot samples were overwhelmingly nested terminal shadow -> guidance_update -> terminal_predict.

implementedContract.hardLoop: Once taem_exec owns the vehicle, dynamic_prediction is cache-only and contains no call to predictor_simulate_terminal_shadow_ensemble.
implementedContract.advisoryWorker: A dedicated worker snapshots terminal state under the controller mutex, releases it, executes the full ensemble off the command path, then conditionally publishes a still-relevant result.
implementedContract.completionRelativeCadence: The next terminal advisory interval is measured from the freshest KSP UT observed when the previous ensemble completes, preventing immediate catch-up reruns after a slow solve.

offlineTiming.interpretation: The expensive computation remains intentionally available for advisory fidelity, but it is no longer on the TAEM command-critical path.

architectureAssertions: full terminal shadow ensemble is absent from dynamic_prediction
the only full ensemble call is in terminal_prediction_worker
controller mutex is released before ensemble execution
worker publication requires current terminal ownership and non-stale request UT

nextLiveMetrics.primaryAcceptance: TAEM must show no repeated multi-second control-loop stalls attributable to advisory prediction; no terminal advisory computation may appear inside guidance/apply latency.
nextLiveMetrics.diagnosticTarget: Normal TAEM loopWallDelta should remain near the pre-pathology ~100 ms cadence; investigate any isolated >1 s tick and treat any repeated >=2 s TAEM ticks as a failure.

liveKspValidation: Not performed by this offline lane; terminal-guidance-live-loop retains exclusive vessel control.
